nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Core.Raux.Rcompare_half_l_spec. Triple-shaped. The carrier is (Rcompare (x/2) y, Rcompare x (2*y)), so the reading is Rcompare (x / 2) y = Rcompare x (2 * y), the same statement over the exact-name counterpart Rcompare. nodes.name: Rcompare_half_r

The carrier is (Rcompare x (y/2), Rcompare (2*x) y), so the reading is Rcompare x (y / 2) = Rcompare (2 * x) y, the same as Coq over the Rcompare counterpart. The equation is independent of the encoding. Verified in V.lean.

nodes.name: Rcompare_sqr
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Core.Raux.Rcompare_sqr_spec. Triple-shaped. The carrier is (Rcompare (x*x) (y*y), Rcompare |x| |y|), so the reading is Rcompare (x * x) (y * y) = Rcompare |x| |y|, identical to Coq over the Rcompare counterpart. The equation is independent of the encoding. A private direct version, Rcompare_sqr_run_eq, also exists. Verified in V.lean.

nodes.name: Rmin_compare
nodes.note: Triple-shaped. The carrier is (min x y, Rcompare x y), so the reading is min x y = if Rcompare x y = -1 then x else if Rcompare x y = 0 then x else y. Coq matches on the comparison constructors (Gt => y | _ => x). Lean branches on ℤ codes. The two agree under the legacy Lt = -1 / Eq = 0 / Gt = 1 encoding, because Lean's Rcompare only returns -1, 0 or 1. The difference is the encoding of the comparison value, not the math. Reading verified in V.lean.

nodes.name: rndNA

Lean writes `Znearest ZnearestA` inline, and valid_rnd_NA is stated on that term. Lean's own `Generic_fmt.ZnearestA` is the tie-break choice function `fun t : Int => decide (0 ≤ t)` of type ℤ → Bool. That is not Coq's ZnearestA, which is Znearest (Zle_bool 0) : R -> Z. Port plan: In FloatSpec/src/Core/Generic_fmt.lean next to valid_rnd_NA (~line 3580), add `@[flocq_source "src/Core/Generic_fmt.v" 2423 "rndNA"] noncomputable abbrev rndNA : ℝ → Int := Znearest ZnearestA`. Its Valid_rnd instance follows from valid_rnd_NA or valid_rnd_N. Be careful with the ZnearestA name collision described above.

Lean namespaces constructors under the inductive (negligible_exp_prop.negligible_None) and makes fexp implicit, which is why the exact-name check fails.

nodes.name: negligible_Some
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Core.Ulp.negligible_exp_prop.negligible_Some. This is the same constructor. `∀ n ≤ fexp n, P` is Lean's binder notation for `∀ n, n ≤ fexp n → P`, and fexp is implicit.

nodes.name: negligible_exp_prop_ind
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Core.Ulp.negligible_exp_prop.rec. This is the kernel-generated Prop eliminator. Lean's recursor has a dependent motive and an implicit index, while Coq's _ind uses a non-dependent P. Setting motive := fun o _ => P o gives Coq's statement exactly. A compiled check confirmed this: `fun _ P h1 h2 _ t => negligible_exp_prop.rec (motive := fun o _ => P o) h1 h2 t` typechecks against Coq's verbatim type. With definitional proof irrelevance, the two forms are interderivable. casesOn and recOn are also generated.

nodes.name: negligible_exp_prop_sind
nodes.note: Rocq-only, not applicable to Lean (SProp eliminator). Rocq auto-generates this eliminator into the SProp sort (definitionally proof-irrelevant propositions). Lean 4 has no SProp universe; its Prop is already definitionally proof-irrelevant. So a separate SProp scheme cannot exist, and Prop elimination is covered by negligible_exp_prop.rec.

nodes.name: ZnearestE
nodes.note: Missing from the Lean port (discovery 2026-09-22; port difficulty: trivial). This is an exported, globally visible notation, and Flocq's round_NE_pt, round_NE_opp and round_NE_abs are stated with it. FloatSpec has no declaration naming it. Every use in Round_NE.lean, Calc/Round.lean and Pff inlines `Znearest (fun t => !(decide (2 ∣ t)))`. The inlined choice matches Coq's `negb (Z.even x)`; a compiled check showed `!(decide (2 ∣ t)) = !(decide (Even t))`. Calc.Round.nearestEvenMode wraps the same function in a Lean-only Mode structure marked flocq_local, so it is not a counterpart. Private helpers such as ZnearestE_opp use the name only in their own identifiers. Port plan: In FloatSpec/src/Core/Round_NE.lean (namespace FloatSpec.Core.RoundNE, before section ParityAuxiliary), add `@[flocq_source "src/Core/Round_NE.v" 26 "ZnearestE"] noncomputable abbrev ZnearestE : ℝ → Int := FloatSpec.Core.Generic_fmt.Znearest (fun t : Int => !(decide (2 ∣ t)))`. Its Valid_rnd instance comes from Generic_fmt.valid_rnd_N. Optionally restate round_NE_pt, round_NE_opp and round_NE_abs and set nearestEvenMode.rnd := ZnearestE so statements read like the source.

nodes.note: Missing from the Lean port (discovery 2026-09-22; port difficulty: trivial). Coq's FIX_format is a one-constructor Inductive and FIX_spec is its constructor. Proofs build it with the anonymous constructor ⟨f, hx, he⟩, as FIX_format_zero does. rg finds no FIX_spec and no intro-style lemma anywhere in FloatSpec. Port plan: Add to FloatSpec/src/Core/FIX.lean after the FIX_format def (line ~61): @[flocq_source "src/Core/FIX.v" 35 "FIX_spec"] theorem FIX_spec (beta : Int) [ValidRadix beta] (x : ℝ) (f : FlocqFloat beta) (hx : x = F2R f) (he : f.Fexp = emin) : FIX_format emin beta x := ⟨f, hx, he⟩. Proofs eliminate it with obtain ⟨f, h1, h2⟩ (Exists.elim/And.rec). The statement can be written in Lean but nothing states it, so it is missing, not not-applicable. The Lean port encodes FLX_format as an ∃-def, so no named introduction rule exists. FloatSpec's Zpower is 0 for negative exponents, which matches Z.pow. The Lean FLX_format_spec is not this constructor: it is a legacy Id Hoare triple stating FLX_format = generic_format (FLX_exp prec) under [Prec_gt_0 prec]. rg finds no FLX_spec. Port plan: FloatSpec/src/Core/FLX.lean after the FLX_format def (line ~96): @[flocq_source "src/Core/FLX.v" 40 "FLX_spec"] theorem FLX_spec (beta : Int) [ValidRadix beta] (x : ℝ) (f : FlocqFloat beta) (hx : x = F2R f) (hm : |f.Fnum| < Zpower beta prec) : FLX_format prec beta x := ⟨f, hx, hm⟩. Do not add [Prec_gt_0 prec]: the Coq constructor does not depend on it. This typechecked in scratch P.lean.

nodes.name: FLX_format_ind
nodes.note: Missing from the Lean port (discovery 2026-09-22; port difficulty: trivial). This is Coq's automatically generated non-dependent eliminator for Inductive FLX_format. The Lean ∃-def is eliminated by obtain/Exists.elim, and no named declaration states this curried eliminator. Port plan: FloatSpec/src/Core/FLX.lean: @[flocq_source "src/Core/FLX.v" 39 "FLX_format_ind"] theorem FLX_format_ind (beta : Int) [ValidRadix beta] (x : ℝ) (P : Prop) (h : ∀ f : FlocqFloat beta, x = F2R f → |f.Fnum| < Zpower beta prec → P) : FLX_format prec beta x → P := fun ⟨f, h1, h2⟩ => h f h1 h2. This typechecked in scratch P.lean.

nodes.name: Fnum
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Pff.Source.float.Fnum. This is the first projection of Pff's radix-free float record. FloatSpec/src/Pff/SourceFacade.lean line 23 declares `structure float where Fnum : Int; Fexp : Int` under @[flocq_source "src/Pff/Pff.v" 1134 "float"]. The fields have the same order and types, the structure has no parameters, and the constructor mk : ℤ → ℤ → float matches Coq's Float. Only the structure carries an anchor, not its projection, which is why the atlas reports Fnum as unaddressed. The integrated root abbrev `float beta := FlocqFloat beta` is radix-indexed. The Source facade is the exact counterpart.

nodes.name: vNum
nodes.note: The codomain differs: Coq returns `positive`, Lean returns ℕ. Positivity lives in a separate field, vNum_pos : 0 < vNum, of the same structure, which is anchored as @[flocq_source "src/Pff/Pff.v" 1664 "Fbound"] in SourceFacade.lean line 237. The Lean record is therefore isomorphic to Coq's positive × N record, so this is a representation difference, not a semantic gap: Coq's `Zpos (vNum b)` corresponds to Lean's `(b.vNum : ℤ)`. The integrated carrier, root Fbound, has vNum : Fbound → ℤ with vNum_pos, is further from the source, and is reached through Source.Fbound.toIntegrated.

nodes.name: dExp

nodes.name: FtoRradix
nodes.note: Missing from the Lean port (discovery 2026-09-22; port difficulty: trivial). Many sections in Pff.v declare `Let FtoRradix := FtoR radix`, and those section-local Lets are discharged when their sections close. The one exception is Section Fast (Fast2Sum), which declares `Local Coercion FtoRradix := FtoR radix`. That form is a Definition, so it survives as the global constant Flocq.Pff.Pff.FtoRradix : float -> R, fixed at radix 2 (checked with Print). No Lean declaration names this map: rg finds no FtoRradix and no def with body FtoR 2 or FtoR (beta := 2). The closest unnamed term is `FloatSpec.Pff.Source.FtoR 2 : FloatSpec.Pff.Source.float → ℝ`. Lean's Fast-section theorems (IminusCorrect, IplusOr, Dekker_FTS in Pff.lean) call F2R/FtoR explicitly instead of using a coercion, and Dekker_FTS uses FlocqFloat 2. Port plan: In FloatSpec/src/Pff/SourceFacade.lean after FtoR (line 61): `@[flocq_source "src/Pff/Pff.v" 23047 "FtoRradix"] noncomputable def FtoRradix : float → ℝ := FtoR 2`, plus an unfolding simp lemma `FtoRradix x = FtoR 2 x` (rfl). A scoped `Coe float ℝ` instance through FtoRradix is optional; it would mirror the Local Coercion, but explicit FtoR calls are clearer. No proof obligations follow.

nodes.name: FtoRradix
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): pff_to_R_aux. Same definition. Coq's section coercion FtoRradix := FtoR beta takes the radix and returns IZR Fnum * powerRZ beta Fexp. The Lean local bridge pff_to_R_aux in Pff2FlocqAux.lean takes beta with [ValidRadix beta], which stands for Coq's radix type, and returns F2R f = Fnum * beta ^ Fexp. It plays the coercion's role in every Pff2FlocqAux statement (65 uses), for example format_is_pff_format's `pff_to_R_aux beta f = r`. There are two representational differences. (1) The float carrier is the radix-indexed PffFloat beta (= FlocqFloat beta) rather than Coq's unindexed Pff.float. The whole main Lean Pff port translates Pff.float that way (Pff.lean `abbrev float beta := FlocqFloat beta`, and `FtoR` there is also F2R). (2) Lean registers no Coe instance, so callers apply the function explicitly. The unindexed source-faithful alternative is FloatSpec.Pff.Source.FtoR : ℤ → Source.float → ℝ, which is anchored to Pff.FtoR. Restricted to valid radices, it is exactly FtoRradix and agrees with F2R via Source.FtoR_toCore. nodes.name: inbetween_Exact
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Calc.Bracket.inbetween.inbetween_Exact. Constructor of the Lean inductive inbetween (Bracket.lean:95). The section hypothesis Hdu : d < u is unused by the inductive and absent from the compiled Coq type, and it is also absent in Lean. The premise x = d and the index loc_Exact are identical. nodes.name: inbetween_Inexact
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Calc.Bracket.inbetween.inbetween_Inexact. Constructor of the Lean inductive inbetween (Bracket.lean:96). `(d < x < u)%R` unfolds to `d < x /\ x < u`. Coq's Raux.Rcompare returns a comparison. Lean's Raux.Rcompare returns Int codes, so the constructor instead uses FloatSpec.Calc.Bracket.compare, which is Ordering-valued: `if x < y then lt else if x > y then gt else eq`. That is the same function as Coq's Rcompare, which cases on total_order_T. V.lean compiled the trichotomy equivalence (compare = lt iff x<y, = eq iff x=y, = gt iff y<x), so the premise is the same proposition.

nodes.name: prec_lt_emax
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): Prec_lt_emax.prec_lt_emax. The Coq class is a definitional singleton class, so its method prec_lt_emax is the projection Prec_lt_emax prec emax -> prec < emax. The Lean class (src/Compat.lean:78) is a one-field Prop structure whose projection has exactly that type. The only difference is binder explicitness: Coq's Arguments makes prec and emax explicit, Lean makes them implicit. The class carries no extra field; the Lean docstring says emax_ge_2 is a separate theorem derived from Prec_gt_0.

nodes.name: emin
nodes.note: Rocq-only, not applicable to Lean (section-local notation in Section Binary). This is a section-local Coq Notation, not a definition. It abbreviates the Rocq Corelib constant SpecFloat.emin, which lives in Corelib.Floats.SpecFloat, not in Flocq. The Lean port writes the unfolded body `3 - emax - prec` inline everywhere: BinarySingleNaN.lean uses FLT_exp (3 - emax - prec) prec, emin_lt_emax states (3 - emax - prec) < emax, and bounded_ge_emin uses bpow 2 (3 - emax - prec). This matches SpecFloat.emin prec emax = 3 - emax - prec. No Lean declaration named emin exists (rg found none).

nodes.name: fexp
nodes.note: Rocq-only, not applicable to Lean (section-local notation in Section Binary). This is a section-local Coq Notation that abbreviates the Corelib constant SpecFloat.fexp, not a Flocq definition. The Lean port writes `FLT_exp (3 - emax - prec) prec` inline throughout BinarySingleNaN.lean and Binary.lean, including canonical_mantissa and the shr/round code. I compiled `example : FLT_exp (3 - emax - prec) prec e = max (e - prec) (3 - emax - prec) := rfl`, which confirms that the inline term is definitionally SpecFloat.fexp's body. No Lean constant named fexp exists for this format.

nodes.name: fexp_correct
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Core.FLT.FLT_exp_valid. Inconsistent with the sibling Binary.v:fexp_correct@3461, which is classified renamed-match against the same Lean instance. coqc shows the two Coq constants have the identical compiled type and body. The BSN explanation's claim that the Lean instance is 'strictly more general' is wrong. SpecFloat.fexp prec emax = fun e => Z.max (e - prec) (3 - emax - prec), and the Lean FLT_exp prec emin e := max (e - prec) emin. Because emax ranges over all of Z, the map emax ↦ 3 - emax - prec is a bijection, so the two statements imply each other. Both directions compiled in critic/V2.lean. (1) `FLT_exp_valid prec (3 - emax - prec)` inhabits `Valid_exp (fun e => max (e - prec) (3 - emax - prec))` definitionally. (2) From the Coq-shaped statement, instantiating emax := 3 - prec - emin and rewriting by ring gives `Valid_exp (FLT_exp prec emin)`. `inferInstance` also resolves `Valid_exp (FLT_exp (3 - emax - prec) prec)`, which is the inline spelling BinarySingleNaN.lean uses. So the difference is only which integer parameter is quantified, not the content of the proposition.

nodes.name: B754_nan

nodes.name: B754_finite
nodes.note: The Lean constructor encodes the mantissa as m : ℕ with a separate 0 < m proof. Coq uses m : positive, so the argument lists differ premise for premise: Lean has an extra positivity premise and a ℕ carrier. The encodings are isomorphic, since positive corresponds to {m : ℕ // 0 < m}. Lean's specFloat_bounded is canonical_mantissa && decide (e ≤ emax - prec), where canonical_mantissa is e == FLT_exp (3-emax-prec) prec (Zdigits 2 m + e). Coq has Z.eqb (fexp (Zpos (digits2_pos m) + e)) e && Z.leb e (emax - prec). These agree for m > 0 because digits2_pos equals Zdigits 2 on positives. The raw constructor is therefore not source-shaped, but it is semantically equivalent. In contrast, Binary.binary_float.B754_finite (Binary.lean:480) already uses FloatSpec.Core.Zaux.Positive.

nodes.name: binary_float_rect
nodes.note: Lean's universe-polymorphic rec (motive in Sort u) subsumes the Type-valued eliminator, and the zero, infinity and NaN minor premises match. The finite minor premise inherits the B754_finite carrier difference: it quantifies over m : ℕ with 0 < m and specFloat_bounded, not over m : positive with SpecFloat.bounded. The two are isomorphic but not premise for premise.

nodes.name: binary_float_ind
nodes.note: Lean's rec with motive in Sort 0 (Prop) is the induction principle. The finite case quantifies over (m : ℕ) (0 < m) (specFloat_bounded m e = true), not (m : positive) (SpecFloat.bounded m e = true). This is the same isomorphic carrier difference as B754_finite.

nodes.name: binary_float_rec
nodes.note: Lean's rec at Sort 1 (= Type, which plays the role of Set) covers the Set-valued eliminator. The finite minor premise has the same ℕ-plus-positivity versus positive difference as B754_finite.

nodes.name: binary_float_sind
nodes.note: Rocq-only, not applicable to Lean (SProp eliminator). This is the SProp eliminator Rocq generates automatically for every inductive. Lean 4 has no SProp universe, so it cannot have an analogue. BinarySingleNaNFloat.rec with a Prop motive covers the Prop-valued eliminator (see binary_float_ind).

nodes.name: F754_zero
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): full_float.F754_zero. Checked with coqc and lake env lean. The constructor of the exact-carrier Lean inductive `full_float` (FloatSpec/src/IEEE754/Binary.lean:20, marked `-- Coq: full_float`) has the same argument. The atlas missed it only because Lean puts constructors in the inductive's namespace. Do not confuse it with the older `FullFloat.F754_zero` on the Nat-payload compatibility carrier.

nodes.name: F754_infinity
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): full_float.F754_infinity. This is the same constructor of the exact `full_float` inductive in Binary.lean:20, with one Bool sign argument. It is namespaced as `full_float.F754_infinity`.

nodes.name: F754_nan
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): full_float.F754_nan. The payload uses `FloatSpec.Core.Zaux.Positive` (constructors xH/xO/xI, verified with #print), which mirrors Coq `positive`. The arguments match one for one. The older `FullFloat.F754_nan : Bool → ℕ → FullFloat` is a separate Nat-payload compatibility type and is not the counterpart.

nodes.name: F754_finite
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): full_float.F754_finite. The arguments are the same: sign, a positive mantissa (as `Zaux.Positive`) and an integer exponent. This is on the exact `full_float` inductive, not the Nat-mantissa `FullFloat`.

nodes.name: full_float_rect
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): full_float.rec. This is Coq's generated eliminator into Type. Lean generates one recursor, `full_float.rec`, whose motive can live in any `Sort u`. At `Sort (u+1)` it has the same four case premises and the same conclusion. The motive is implicit in Lean and explicit in Coq, which is only a binder difference. `full_float.recOn` and `full_float.casesOn` are also available.

nodes.name: full_float_ind
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): full_float.rec. This is the induction principle. Lean's `full_float.rec` with motive in `Sort 0 = Prop` has exactly these case premises and this conclusion. Lean does not make a separate `.ind` constant; the one Sort-polymorphic recursor covers it, and the `induction` and `cases` tactics use it.

nodes.name: full_float_rec
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): full_float.rec. This is the Set-valued eliminator. Coq's Set corresponds to Lean's `Type` (Sort 1), and `full_float.rec` at that level has the same premises and conclusion.

nodes.name: full_float_sind
nodes.note: Rocq-only, not applicable to Lean (SProp eliminator). Changed for consistency. 13 of the 16 SProp-eliminator items in this batch are classified not-applicable: the Zaux/Bracket/Ulp/FIX/FLX/FLXN/FLT/FTZ _sind items, BinarySingleNaN.binary_float_sind and mode_sind. The reason given there applies here too. The compiled Coq type quantifies over P : full_float -> SProp. Lean has no SProp sort, so that type cannot be stated. The Prop-motive instance of full_float.rec is exactly the compiled full_float_ind, which is already mapped to full_float.rec, so claiming it again for _sind double-counts one Lean instance. Nothing needs porting. If the orchestrator prefers the opposite convention (Lean's definitionally proof-irrelevant Prop as the SProp analogue, so renamed-match), flip all 16 _sind items together, and note that FIX/FLX/FLXN/FLT/FTZ_format_sind would then become missing alongside their _ind.

nodes.note: Rocq-only, not applicable to Lean (section-local notation in Section Binary). Binary.v:153 is a parsing-only Notation abbreviating the Corelib constant `SpecFloat.fexp prec emax`. No Flocq constant survives the Section. Lean spells it as `FLT_exp (3 - emax - prec) prec`, where the root abbrev `FLT_exp emin prec` equals `FloatSpec.Core.FLT.FLT_exp prec emin` and `FLT_exp prec emin e = max (e - prec) emin`. That is definitionally `max (e - prec) (3 - emax - prec)`, the same as SpecFloat.fexp. It is used in `canonical_mantissa`/`specFloat_bounded` in Binary.lean:255-263 and throughout BinarySingleNaN.lean. This is a Notation artifact.

nodes.name: fexp_correct
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): FloatSpec.Core.FLT.FLT_exp_valid. The Coq Instance is literally `FLT_exp_valid (emin prec emax) prec`, a specialization of the general FLT instance. Lean has no separately named specialized instance. Instead, the general Lean instance `FloatSpec.Core.FLT.FLT_exp_valid` (FLT.lean:100) resolves it automatically, and I checked this: with `[Prec_gt_0 prec]` in context, `inferInstance : Valid_exp (FLT_exp (3 - emax - prec) prec)` elaborates to `@FloatSpec.Core.FLT.FLT_exp_valid prec (3 - emax - prec) inst`. That is the same term as the Coq body, and its type is definitionally `Valid_exp (SpecFloat.fexp prec emax)`. The premises match: both need only Prec_gt_0 prec, since Coq dropped the unused Prec_lt_emax context. The only difference is the Lean argument order (prec emin versus Coq's emin prec).

nodes.name: B754_nan
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): binary_float.B754_nan. The fields match: sign, a positive payload (`Zaux.Positive`) and a payload-validity proof `nan_pl prec pl = true`. Lean's `nan_pl` (Binary.lean:239) is `Zlt_bool (digits2_pos (positiveToNat pl)) prec`, the carrier of Coq's `(Z.pos (digits2_pos pl) <? prec)`, and it is the same-named port of Binary.v's nan_pl.

nodes.name: B754_finite
nodes.note: Counterpart under another name (discovery 2026-09-22): binary_float.B754_finite. The fields match: sign, positive mantissa, integer exponent, and a boundedness proof. Lean states the proof on `specFloat_bounded (positiveToNat m) e`, which is `(e == FLT_exp (3-emax-prec) prec (Zdigits 2 m + e)) && decide (e ≤ emax - prec)`. I compiled a scratch proof (Q3.lean) that this equals Coq's shape `(FLT_exp (3-emax-prec) prec (digits2_pos (positiveToNat m) + e) == e) && decide (e ≤ emax - prec)`, using `Zpos_digits2_pos` and `positiveToNat_pos`. So the premise is the same proposition as `SpecFloat.bounded prec emax m e = true`, written on the Nat carrier.

roots.rule: Definitions (roots) shows every definition and every theorem that is not both proven in the Lean snapshot and spot-checked by Claude against pinned Flocq. Proven, spot-checked theorems are folded into the nearest visible declarations they depend on. Rocq-only declarations (n/a) are hidden and listed on their module’s strip.

caveats: Module order comes from coqdep -sort, not -v/-V.
Declaration order comes from compiled .glob source positions.
Solid edges come from dpdgraph when available; identifier-to-source mapping is approximate.
Lean matching is approximate; use the shown source to decide.
Green marks checked slices: the port review queue, its review ledger, or Claude spot checks. Amber is a match awaiting review. Red includes separate native proof obligations.

Grey (Rocq-only, n/a) marks SProp eliminators and section-local notations that the port’s classification finds nothing to port for; progress ratios exclude them. Only declarations with no Lean match by name or anchor are classified, so an eliminator or notation whose name a Lean declaration reuses keeps that match’s colour.
“Proven” means the selected Lean counterpart has no explicit sorry and no proof-debt entry; FloatSpec’s own check_proof_debts.py verifies that no other declaration transitively depends on sorry.
